To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of cerebral oximery during cardiac surgery may be useful in the prediction of cognitive dysfunction and the patients' outcome following the surgery.

(1) cognitive dysfunction after valvular heart surgeries is common; (2) cerebral oximetry can help identify patients at risk of developing cognitive dysfunction; (3) cognitive dysfunction after heart surgery is associated with worse patients' outcome; (4) the use of cerebral oximety can help to improve the outcome after heart surgery.
cerebral oximetry is useful in the prediction of cognitive dysfunction following cardiac surgery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the relationship between the use of cerebral oximmetry during valvular surgery, cognitive dysfunction, and patients outcome.
the study of the effects of valvular heart disease on the cognitive functioning of the patient.
the prediction of cognitive function and the role of CBF monitoring in the context of cardiac surgery with CPB.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of cerebral oximery during valvular surgery is not yet recommended as a routine procedure.
there are no data to support the routine use of CBF monitoring during cardiac surgery.
the use of the Cerebral oximeter during cardiac surgery is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of cerebral oximety monitoring is a useful adjunct to clinical assessment and monitoring of cerebral perfusion during valvular heart surgical procedures.
the use of the Cerebral State Index (CSI) is a useful adjunct to clinical assessment of cognitive dysfunction following valvular surgery.
cerebral oxygenation monitoring during valvular heart surgeries can be useful in predicting postoperative cognitive dysfunction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the data from a single EEG recording to predict the cognitive outcome of a patient after cardiac surgery.
the use of cerebral oximery during cardiac surgery is not associated with improved outcomes.
the use of the cerebral oximeter is associated with improved patient outcomes following cardiac surgery.
